newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila mills jump into market as U.S. prices dip.
newsitem.headline: Manila mills jump into market as U.S. prices dip.

text.p: Philippine flour mills sent out a series of tender invitations to wheat suppliers on Wednesday after U.S. prices slid for the fourth consecutive session, dealers said.
Traders said they received price inquiries for a total 90,000 tonnes of wheat and 7,500 tonnes of soybean, all for June shipment.

One mill bought 7,500 tonnes of western white wheat at $4.02 a bushel FOB from the U.S. Pacific northwest port and 7,500 tonnes of soybean at $8.92 a bushel, traders who joined the tender told Reuters.
The company decided to defer buying another 7,500 tonnes of dark northern spring wheat with 14 percent protein content due to high prices, said a senior Manila trader.
Results of the other tenders were not immediately known.
Executives of Philippine flour mills said they were expecting lower prices on Wednesday.
"But we got higher quotes than we expected in today's bidding because of reports that Pakistan was set to buy 330,000 tonnes of wheat tonight," an executive at one of the flour mills told Reuters.
Traders said some firms that had deferred buying were betting the entire Pakistani order would not go to the U.S.
Pakistan was expected to decide later on Wednesday on the tender of U.S. or Australian soft white wheat for shipment between May 20 and June 10.
"Everybody's watching developments in Pakistan," said a Manila trader.
Manila grains traders said if Australia won the bulk of the Pakistani order, U.S. wheat prices would soften further.
